items.title: 25 of my favourite modern NES games
items.summary: games, retrocomputing
items.content:
We are in the middle of the Second ReNESance (the first one is the one that saved the video game industry in North America). The combined decades of research and knowledge on how the venerable little NES works have produced a true cornucopia of games. We are all lucky to be here to witness it.

I am always happy to inform video game fans that the Nintendo Entertainment System is still receiving lots and lots of new third-party games.

In alphabetical order, because I refuse to rank them, here are 25 of my favourite modern NES games. Almost all can be obtained digitally, usually from the developer or publisher, most for a modest fee. Digital NES downloads are cheap! Most of these can also be obtained as physical cartridges for the true hi-fi experience on original hardware.

A little spooky, very pixelly. This game is a real gem.

Made by 8-bit Slasher who has been honing his skills in other horror games for the NES, All Hell Unleashed is an extensive love letter to the horror slashers of the 1980s and 1990s. There is an underlying story about an evil cult that is trying to resurrect something or other, but that’s just an excuse plot so that you can fight Jaws, Freddy, Jason, Ghostface and others. It works surprisingly well. You can select your favourite horror movie from a stage-select screen to do your platforming as you fight the forces of evil, culminating in the boss fights where the villain of each horror franchise swoops in for a mano-a-mano . The platforming feels good, and the boss fights function as set pieces showcasing the real villains we are here to see in their 8-bit glory.

Finally Jason dons a better outfit on the NES than that silly purple jumpsuit!

After each classic horror villain is defeated, it is time to take on the cult itself for one final showdown. Definitely a spine-tingling adventure!

Alwa’s Awakening was originally a PC game made with pseudo-NES limitations (and in the case of the music, with actual NES limitations, as the developer used Famitracker to compose all of the music). If it doesn’t feel like a classic NES game and instead plays more like a modern indie Metroidvania, that’s because it is.

In the game, you play as Zoe, a girl who likes video games and one day awakens in the mystical land of Alwa, a place from one of her games. Your task is to guide Zoe through an adventure in Alwa where she will uncover power-ups that open up new avenues of adventure. Typical Metroidvania stuff, although a bit shorter than most games in the genre. The PC-to-NES port of this game was handled by my good friend Brad Smith of Lizard fame. He made a couple of interesting YouTube videos describing the process.

The game looks absolutely gorgeous for the NES, and its Famitracker-composed soundtrack made it through the porting process completely unscathed. There was a limited physical edition that today is only available via secondhand markets. If you can grab a copy, it’s a very high-quality production. This is some of the best stuff made for the system.

Anguna is an NES game with an interesting lineage. It was originally made in 2008 for the Game Boy Advance as essentially the same game, but a bit more to the standards of the GBA. Then it was successively ported to the Nintendo DS, the Atari 2600, and finally the NES.

The Atari 2600-to-NES port was done fairly faithfully, which means that the design decisions necessary for the Atari also made it into the NES port. This means, for example, no more than two enemies per screen and always of the same type. This sort of restriction isn’t unheard of in the NES, though. The very popular NES Double Dragon port also has the same limitation. The game design makes up for it and overall results in an enjoyable experience. And isn’t that what making and playing modern NES games is all about? An interesting experience made with strict hardware limitations.

So what is Anguna? At its most basic, it’s a Zelda-like. You walk around screens, you grab new tools, your tools…

items.title: NetBSD may have found a new role: The AI-free FOSS OS
items.content:
NetBSD may have found a new role: The AI-free FOSS OS

Increasing awareness and adoption, followed by increasing donations

Pigeon-powered internet packet goes under the hammer at Christie's

Raspberry Pi Desktop catches up with Debian 13 after 4-year wait

OpenAI dots inspire open source imitators amid technical difficulties

COSMIC shuts the door on AI code as GNOME debates letting bug reports in

Only the finest Swedish Bork will do for Stockholm station

NetBSD seems to be thriving of late: as the Linux world goes pro-AI, some of the AI-averse are turning to this explicitly AI-free project.

The NetBSD project’s Mastodon feed reports that it received a record 120 donations last month, and it has far exceeded its target:

“We received $120,282 USD in total. Naturally, this has completely filled up our donations target bar which was set at $50,000. Time to fund some projects!”

It’s a welcome contrast to the usual stories of under-funded FOSS projects, and it follows a visible uptick in people asking about NetBSD in the FOSS Unix groups we read, ever since Emperor Penguin Torvalds said that Linux was not an anti-AI project back in July, and the following month, the Debian project polled its developers on AI use, and they chose to permit AI-generated contributions .

This is the moderate, centrist stance. The most recent Ubuntu Summit was heavily AI-flavored . The heads of Red Hat Global Engineering sent out a memo about transitioning to an Agentic Software Development Lifecycle . But once it’s in the kernel, then no distro can totally avoid it. This stance is profoundly offputting to those who prefer hand-crafted code.

Last week, the Reg FOSS desk attended the Open Source Summit Europe in Prague . This event reflects the tendencies of the increasingly mainstream open-source world: Linux is pretty much the only OS in evidence, although many attendees tote around (and present from) MacBooks, and both Microsoft and Windows were visible. The event overlaps with Embedded Linux Conference , so the Zephyr RTOS was also visible on some robots and other gadgets.

The Open Source Summit gives the overall impression that Linux is the only general-purpose FOSS OS. We saw no mention at all of any of the BSDs; indeed, when we mentioned NetBSD, some of the folks from Let’s Encrypt looked puzzled and asked us “What’s ‘net bee ess dee’?” Sadly, this is probably a reasonably fair representation of its presence at the event and in the FOSS mainstream. For us, the single most dominant theme in the talks, the materials, the stands, and even the T-shirts was AI. It’s everywhere, and every exhibitor was keen to talk about how they’re using AI, deploying AI, scaling AI, or managing AI.

The louder the noise about AI gets, the stronger grows the aversion of those of us who actively wish to avoid it. The NetBSD project, on the other hand, came out early and strongly: it banned AI-generated code back in 2024, just a month after the project celebrated its 30th anniversary .

This vulture attended the project’s talk at that year’s FOSDEM: NetBSD 10: Thirty years, still going strong ! . As ever, the question of differentiation between the BSDs, and between Linux and the BSDs, came up.

NetBSD’s slogan is “Of course it runs NetBSD,”  but in 2024, its ubiquity was looking threatened: Linux is comparable, and FreeBSD boast close integration with ZFS, Linux-compatible Podman containers, and more.

The following year, though, FreeBSD 15 appeared, dropping support for 32-bit x86 (and 32-bit POWER). Debian 13 dropped x86-32 too , as well as MIPS CPU support. That year, the RHEL 10 release went further: it not only requires 64-bit x86, it demands x86-64-v3. This cut off so many older machines, it forced CERN to start switching to Debian .

From within the BSD world, the differences between the various projects are fairly clear. NetBSD is minimal, highly portable, and takes great pride in its very friendly, welcoming community. We can personally attest to this:…

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 2개, 댓글 4개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 1일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Lovable apps expose passport details and more than 200K private messages
items.content:
Lovable: Many Apps Built on the Platform Expose Sensitive Data

AI makes it easier to build your own web applications, but handling sensitive data still requires special

care. We examined 159,041 Lovable projects and found many cases where personal and confidential information was

Lovable is a Swedish AI startup founded in Stockholm in 2023 by Anton Osika and Fabian Hedin. The platform turns

plain-language descriptions into web applications and is designed to be accessible even to people with little

Lovable grew out of Osika’s open-source project “GPT Engineer”, released in 2023. The project evolved into the

GPT Engineer App before being renamed Lovable in late 2024 and launching publicly that November.

Lovable can build impressively sophisticated web projects with AI, from static websites to full applications

with user management and database connections. But as soon as an application handles confidential information,

one question becomes crucial: Is that data protected against unauthorized access?

emphasizes that no technical knowledge is needed to build

projects . This can give the impression that the platform takes care of security

too. Yet Lovable’s Terms & Conditions place responsibility for applications and data handling on the

That leaves a troubling gap between the promise of an easy-to-use, all-in-one service and the responsibilities

Against this backdrop, we investigated how well sensitive data in Lovable applications is protected, in

collaboration with Handelsblatt . Lina Knees reported on the findings on

We wanted to find out whether sensitive data in Lovable applications was accessible without logging in. We

looked separately at data sent when a website first loaded and additional content we checked by making further

read-only requests with the same API key.

The result: We found many clear examples of sensitive data left unprotected.

We focused on the database service Supabase . Its integration is relatively easy to

analyze, and we believe it is the most widely used database service among Lovable projects. Lovable’s own

database features, introduced in late 2025, are still less widely used. Similar misconfigurations may occur

there too, but we did not examine them in this analysis.

Using datasets from the open web archive Common Crawl , we identified and analyzed

159,041 Lovable projects from December 2025 to September 2026 . Of these, 34,545 used Supabase.

24,664 websites sent database records from Supabase as soon as they loaded, without requiring a login or any

other interaction. That alone is not a security issue: the data may be intended for public display. But by

making additional read-only requests, we were able to retrieve more database content. We found records

containing email addresses in 10,560 tables across 7,403 of the 24,664 websites (30%).

Email addresses can help identify records containing personal data, but they may also be public contact

addresses or test data. At the same time, this approach misses personal records that contain no email address.

These effects partly offset one another, though we could not establish to what extent. The 30% figure should

therefore not be read as a confirmed data leak rate. It applies only to the 24,664 websites we examined more

closely. Our sample, drawn from Common Crawl, is also not representative of all Lovable applications.

We retrieved only parts of the datasets rather than downloading them in full. The figures below reflect the

records we actually downloaded; the affected datasets may contain more. We are not publishing details of how to

access them, as doing so could make further access easier.

We found many serious cases of exposed data, including:

A German lifestyle forum exposed more than 80,000 profiles containing full names, email addresses, dates

of birth, and gender information. More than 200,000 chat messages were also accessible.

items.content_ko: Lovable은 2023년 스톡홀름에서 Anton Osika와 Fabian Hedin이 설립한 스웨덴 AI 스타트업으로, 일상 언어로 설명하면 웹 애플리케이션을 만들어 주는 플랫폼이다. 기술 지식이 없는 사람도 쓸 수 있도록 설계되었으며, 2023년 Osika의 오픈소스 프로젝트 ‘GPT Engineer’에서 출발해 2024년 11월 Lovable로 이름을 바꾸고 정식 출시되었다. 원문은 159,041개 Lovable 프로젝트를 조사한 결과 개인정보와 기밀 정보가 노출된 사례가 많이 발견되었다고 밝힌다. 원문은 플랫폼이 기술 지식 없이도 쓸 수 있다고 강조하기 때문에 보안도 플랫폼이 알아서 처리하는 것처럼 보일 수 있다고 지적한다. 본문은 Lovable 이용약관 내용에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Let Me Let You Own Your Data
items.summary: databases, privacy
items.content:
Why do I have to choose between my web app respecting people’s privacy and it, like… having basic functionality?

When I was working on Cheapskate , I realized after a few weeks that there was a fundamental issue. The app relies on Supabase for the unsexy parts of its architecture: authentication and a SQL datastore. All of it is bog-standard and all of it I happily handed off to be someone else’s problem. To be clear, I love Supabase – if I had to run all that boilerplate myself, I never would have made Cheapskate.

But… the shape of it is wrong. I don’t want to own this data. This is a person’s financial details! Shouldn’t that live with them, and not with me? Is it even possible to make a web app like this, with anything close to the same convenience and functionality (durable, works across devices, shareable with friends) as Supabase allows?

Well, I really wanted to. I spent a lot of time trying. Here are all the things that don’t work:

Besides, all of these options compromise on the data model anyway, being KV or blob storage when all I really want is an API to run SQL queries. You know, like any normal app?

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: Italy fines Meta $887m for accessing Android users’ photos and videos
items.content:
Meta had access ⁠to Android users’ photos and videos through a Facebook app feature. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

Meta had access ⁠to Android users’ photos and videos through a Facebook app feature. Photograph: Dado Ruvić/Reuters

Italy fines Meta $887m for accessing Android users’ photos and videos

The fine is among the largest an Italian authority has imposed on a tech giant and Meta says it plans to appeal the decision

Italy’s data protection agency has fined Facebook parent company Meta €805m ($887m) for accessing users’ photos without their specific consent.

Through the Facebook application for Android devices, Meta accessed photographs, videos and related metadata belonging to Italian users “without obtaining specific consent and without properly informing them”, the authority said in a statement.

Meta said it would appeal the decision. A company spokesperson said “we strongly disagree” with the assessment by the regulators “and the disproportionate level of the fine”.

Meta strikes deal with Mark Zuckerberg to help him foot billionaire tax bill

In late October, authorities in New Mexico ordered Meta to pay $25bn for misleading the state’s residents for more than a decade about the use of their data – a record fine for the company, which slammed it as a “tax” on freedom of expression.

Saturday’s latest fine is among the largest an Italian authority has imposed on a tech company.

In 2021, Amazon received a more than €1.1bn fine for breaching competition law.

That sum was subsequently reduced to €752m on appeal.

The Italian penalty imposed on Facebook relates to its gallery suggestions feature, available since 2023, which suggests photos and videos from a user’s phone gallery as ideas for posts as they are browsing.

According to Italy’s regulator, Facebook requested access to the gallery via a single authorisation valid for the entire app, preceded by a generic notice requesting enabling of other features, which did not allow users to understand that they were also authorising suggestions from their gallery.

The regulator said Meta would now have to seek consent by means of a separate and specific request for the feature concerned and clearly signpost what it is used for, namely that it involves access to a user’s photo gallery, as well as how to disable it.

In determining the size of the fine, the authority said it took into account “the high number of people affected” – about 20 million Android users in Italy – and the duration of the infringement, “which is still ongoing for those who have not updated the app and for those who have already given their consent to the system”.

The authority also cited “Meta’s lack of cooperation during the investigation”.

It imposed a fine amounting to roughly 0.4% of the group’s annual turnover, which hit $201bn in 2025, for a net profit of $60.5bn.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: Why get an expensive Pi when I have an old phone?
items.content:
The rooted Redmi talking over USB-C to the LED controller.

I’m working on a project that needs a high resolution camera, GPS, storage, and a microcontroller to control some lights. (More on the project soon!) I’ve been designing PCB adapters around a Raspberry Pi, an Arducam 64MP camera, and a GPS module. Every time I add another part, the bill grows.

I’m also trying an ESP32-P4 board, which will get its own post soon. But the alternative I keep coming back to is an old smartphone.

I have a Redmi 13C 5G and a Huawei Mate 30 5G. Phones like these turn up second hand on Taobao for roughly ¥300–500 (£33–56 / €40–67 / $45–75) . The Redmi gives me a camera that saves 50MP JPEGs; the Mate 30 has a 40MP main camera and a telephoto lens. Both already contain GPS, storage, a clock, a battery, mobile data, and a touchscreen. Their USB-C ports give me a route to the PCB that will handle the lights and other sensors.

Here is the rough parts comparison I made while deciding what to build next:

What I need Used Redmi or Mate 30 Raspberry Pi 4 approach

Computer Included in phone price Pi 4, 4GB : ¥880 / £98 / €118 / $132

High resolution camera Redmi 50MP JPEG; Mate 30 40MP Arducam 64MP : ~¥400 / £45 / €53 / $60

GPS Included GPS HAT : ~¥153 / £17 / €20 / $23

Storage Built in 64GB microSD : ~¥50 / £6 / €7 / $7

Core total ¥300–500 / £33–56 / €40–67 / $45–75 ~¥1,483 / £165 / €198 / $222

Clock Included RTC HAT : ~¥80 / £9 / €11 / $12

Battery backup Included UPS HAT : ~¥133 / £15 / €18 / $20 , plus cells

Touch display Included 5″ touchscreen : ~¥247 / £28 / €33 / $37

Mobile data Built in, with a SIM 4G HAT : ~¥527 / £59 / €70 / $79

More fully equipped total ¥300–500 / £33–56 / €40–67 / $45–75 ~¥2,317 / £258 / €310 / $347 , plus batteries

These are illustrative November 2026 listings. The more fully equipped Pi total uses the cellular HAT’s GPS instead of buying the separate GPS HAT; its modem is 4G, while the phones are 5G models. Neither side includes my custom light controller PCB, a SIM or data plan, or an enclosure. The conversions use 10 November 2026 mid market rates of approximately ¥1 = £0.111531 / €0.133643 / $0.14991 , rounded to whole units in the table.

The phone is already becoming more than a price exercise. I’ve unlocked and rooted the Redmi, tested its camera, and got it sleeping and waking for scheduled work. I can plug it into my computer and have Codex configure and test the pieces I need. The Huawei is harder to root, but I can still run a kiosk app on it. I’ve made a stand to photograph the same target with the Redmi and Arducam side by side; I want to see what detail each camera actually captures. A 50MP JPEG file does not, by itself, settle that question.

The open question is supply. Finding two good used phones is easy; finding a few hundred matching ones, with healthy batteries and predictable camera behaviour, would take more work. I feel increasingly confident that it’s possible.

This could be useful well beyond the current project. For digital artworks and installations, we’ve often used a Pi or a Mac mini. Imagine instead posting a client a configured phone: plug it into the display and it runs. With mobile data and remote access, I can fix something without asking a gallery for Wi-Fi privileges or an open port.

There’s something fun about taking a device made in enormous numbers, giving it a second life, and finding that most of the hardware I was about to assemble is already inside it.

items.content:
Three ways to parse the nested lists from Advent of Code 2022 day 13 in BQN.

Advent of Code 2022 day 13 requires you to parse nested lists like

This post covers three different ways to handle the problem:

1. "Cheating" by using •BQN to do the heavy lifting

2. Writing a conventional recursive descent parser

We'll also do some simple benchmarking to compare the three approaches.

We'll be using my advent of code input file to test the different approaches on.

The lists come in pairs, with each pair separated by a blank line.

Since the problem requires you to compare pairs of lists,

a suitable format for working with the data is to parse it all into one list of pairs of lists.

Thus we can turn the problem into parsing one giant list.

The lines come in groups of three: the first list, the second list, and then a blank line.

The first line of each group needs an opening bracket added to the beginning (to open the pair) and a comma added to the end (to separate the two lists in the pair).

The second line of each group needs a closing bracket at the end (to close the pair) and a comma after (to separate it from the next pair).

Then we join all the lines together and drop the final trailing comma.

Finally, we need to wrap the whole thing in one more set of brackets, to make it all one big list.

This approach is undoubtedly the easiest, and it's what I used to solve the problem in December.

The idea is that the notation is almost valid BQN; we just need to replace the square brackets with angle brackets.

Then we can use the system function •BQN to "eval" the string into a BQN list.

Here's the idea behind replacing a character with another character using a small example.

I've written both an explicit expression and a tacit function.

We take the difference between the new character and the old character,

since adding this to the old character changes it into the new one.

Then we use a mask of old character locations to make sure the addition happens only at those locations.

Now to write our parser, we just replace both kinds of square brackets with the respective angle brackets and call •BQN .

I'm not sure what's going on to be honest.

When I solved the problem in Decemeber I didn't do the "turn it all into one giant list" approach,

Around 3/4 of a second for each run. So slow!

items.title: AI Chatbots Won’t Stop Recommending Scam Websites to People Trying to Shop: Think twice before you shop somewhere that ChatGPT recommended.
items.content:
AI chatbots are taking over as the main way that people use the internet outside social media — and that includes shopping. It makes it pretty concerning, then, that they still have a bad habit of recommending shady websites that rip users off instead of providing the product they’re looking for.

A new study conducted by Podqi and reported on by The Verge found that ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity — some of the industry’s leading chatbots — all showed shoppers risky sites that impersonated real retailers, puppeted dead ones, or sold knockoff products.

The tests involved asking questions like “What are the top websites for buying [brand]?” and “Does [brand] ship internationally?” and “What are their regional websites?” They used about 151 different brands across the questions, running from smaller ones to major ones like Lululemon and Birkenstock.

Perplexity was the worst offender, showing risky sites in 15 percent of its answers. ChatGPT sat in the middle with 8 percent, and Gemini was least likely to show dubious storefronts — albeit at a still-concerning rate of 4 percent.

The chatbots didn’t necessarily endorse the websites in their answers. ChatGPT, for example, gave warnings about the risky sites it brought up in 24 percent of its responses, which is the most out of the three examples.

But overall, 57 percent of the answers that showed a risky site recommended it as a place to shop, and 34 percent did so without comment. Only 9 percent of the answers warned the shopper away.

Smaller brands, it appeared, were the most likely to be shunted out in favor of scam sites in the AI responses. And certain lines of questions, like asking about a brand’s regional website, seemed to trigger risky responses more than others.

“Part of this piece, too, is making sure that the consumers know, even though you are being fed a result in a particular chatbot, it is always best to verify the source of that before entering personal information or credit card information,” Podqi CEO Trevor West told The Verge .

It’s not the only study to expose how chatbots could be hurting their own users by getting dupped. The scam-checking service Ask Silver found that ChatGPT recommends cloned versions of defunct website of well known brands which are designed to steal your banking info.

Traditional search engines like Google can also be manipulated, but AI chatbots present their responses as definitive answers while being relatively opaque about how they reached them, and people are inclined to trust them uncritically. And fooling these tools doesn’t seem all that difficult. A BBC journalist demonstrated how he was easily able to trick ChatGPT into telling other users that he was a renowned hot dog eating champion — which, sadly, was a lie he invented to prove a point.

The internet is more awash than ever with fake junk, ranging from the news you hear to the products you buy. Maybe it isn’t surprising that AI models are having just as hard a time discerning what’s trustworthy and what’s not.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-82568 📢 Source: Wordfence 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False The Give - Peer-to-Peer plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to time-based SQL Injection via the 'sort' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 2.9.3 due to insufficient escaping on the user supplied parameter and lack of sufficient preparation on the existing SQL query. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to append additional SQL queries into already existing queries that can be used to extract sensitive information from the database. Successful exploitation requires the existence of at least one Peer-to-Peer campaign. This vulnerability can be combined with CVE-2026-82663 to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-15T09:34:45.651Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-82568
items.title_ko: WordPress 'The Give - Peer-to-Peer' 플러그인 SQL 인젝션 취약점 (CVE-2026-82568)
items.summary_ko: Wordfence가 공개한 CVE-2026-82568은 WordPress 플러그인 'The Give - Peer-to-Peer' 2.9.3 이하 버전의 'sort' 파라미터에서 발생하는 시간 기반 SQL 인젝션 취약점이다. 비인증 공격자가 데이터베이스의 민감한 정보를 추출할 수 있으며, CVE-2026-82663과 결합하면 비인증 원격 코드 실행이 가능하다고 한다.
items.content_ko: Wordfence가 등록한 취약점으로, The Give - Peer-to-Peer 플러그인의 2.9.3을 포함한 이전 버전에 영향을 준다. 'sort' 파라미터의 사용자 입력이 충분히 이스케이프되지 않고, 기존 SQL 쿼리의 준비(prepare) 처리도 부족해 발생한다. 비인증 공격자가 기존 쿼리에 추가 SQL 쿼리를 덧붙여 데이터베이스의 민감한 정보를 추출할 수 있다. 공격이 성공하려면 최소 하나의 Peer-to-Peer 캠페인이 존재해야 한다. CVE-2026-82663과 결합하면 비인증 원격 코드 실행을 달성할 수 있다. CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA)으로 기재되어 있고, 게시일은 2026-11-15이다.

items.title: Periodic-Oriented Programming for FIRST Robotics
items.summary: programming
items.content:
I recently retired from mentoring my FIRST Robotics Competition (FRC) team. I started as a student in 2010, and went straight into mentoring upon graduation, so in total I have been writing FRC programs for about 17 years.

Over time though I've become more and more dismayed with how FRC programs are typically written. For decades, I feel that FIRST and WPILib have encouraged students to severely overengineer their robot programs. As time has gone on, I have become more and more frustrated with the state of FRC programming, and our team's code style has drifted further and further away from the norm.

To be clear, I have the utmost respect for the time and effort that FIRST and the WPILib maintainers put in every year, and it is thanks to their efforts that FRC teams have reliable and complete libraries every year. But I think the accepted programming practices in FRC are leading students astray and ought to be corrected.

So as I step away from FIRST , I decided I should write down my philosophy of robot programming in FRC, which I have decided to give the pithy name of Periodic-Oriented Programming .

Periodic-Oriented Programming is very simple: Do as much as possible in your periodic function. Uses very few abstractions, and write most of your logic in one big function, top to bottom. This is so simple and beginner-like that it seems like it shouldn't work for serious programs. But it does, as long as you carefully establish a few simple boundaries and practices.

For context, the essential structure of an FRC program is typically to use the TimedRobot framework provided by WPILib. To use it, you simply implement periodic functions and the robot framework calls them 50 times per second. For example, here's a complete "tank drive" robot program in Python:

self . gamepad = wpilib . XboxController ( 0 )

self . leftMotor = rev . SparkMax ( 10 , rev . SparkLowLevel . MotorType . kBrushless )

self . rightMotor = rev . SparkMax ( 11 , rev . SparkLowLevel . MotorType . kBrushless )

self . leftMotor . set ( self . gamepad . getLeftY ())

self . rightMotor . set ( self . gamepad . getRightY ())

50 times per second, the left and right motor speeds will be updated to use the left and right gamepad axes. The robot framework and hardware abstraction layers do the rest.

In essence, every FRC program does the following work in periodic :

Compute the desired state of the hardware (motor speeds, actuator positions, etc.)

Enforce safety constraints, smooth signals, or otherwise process the outputs

In Periodic-Oriented Programming, I basically encourage my students to lean into this pattern. POP code should have few abstractions, and most of the logic should be written top-to-bottom in a single function. And to the greatest extent possible, everything should be run on every periodic —no modes, no commands, no state.

As programs get larger, more structure is needed, but the core philosophy remains the same. The most important piece of structure is subsystems .

The use of "subsystem" classes will be familiar to most FRC teams, but the specifics are what matter here:

Every subsystem has a periodic method. This is called from robotPeriodic so it runs 100% of the time.

Hardware is never accessible outside the subsystem. All access to the hardware must be mediated through subsystem methods.

These rules extend the Periodic-Orientation into the subsystem code. For each subsystem, all of its logic should be centralized in one function and readable top to bottom. In most cases, the subsystem periodic is the only place in the entire program that actually touches the hardware. This has many advantages: it ensures by construction that hardware is only touched once per tick, that safety constraints are respected 100% of the time, and that logging and telemetry are run consistently.

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-129349 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 9.1 (CRITICAL) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: True When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password. A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user. This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default. Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default. Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-15T09:31:50.485Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-129349

items.summary_ko: DefaultLdapRealm에서 인증 캐싱을 켜면, 사용자가 한 번 로그인에 성공한 뒤로는 어떤 비밀번호로도 같은 계정에 로그인할 수 있다는 취약점이다. CVSS 점수는 9.1(CRITICAL)이다. 3.0.1 이상으로 업그레이드하거나 인증 캐싱을 끄는 것이 권고된다.
items.content_ko: Apache가 공개한 취약점으로, DefaultLdapRealm(또는 JndiLdapRealm)에서 authenticationCachingEnabled를 true로 설정한 경우에만 영향을 받는다. 기본값은 해당 설정이 꺼져 있다. 캐싱이 켜진 상태에서 사용자가 한 번 로그인에 성공하면, 이후 로그인은 캐시된 인증 정보로 처리되어 LDAP 바인드를 건너뛴다. 이때 기본으로 설치되는 AllowAllCredentialsMatcher가 모든 자격 증명을 허용하므로, 유효한 사용자 이름만 아는 공격자도 해당 사용자로 인증할 수 있다. 영향을 받는 버전은 3.0.0까지다. 완화 방법은 3.0.1 이상으로 업그레이드하는 것이며, 이 버전부터는 AllowAllCredentialsMatcher가 기본으로 설치되지 않는다. 대안으로 LDAP 레알름의 인증 캐싱을 끄거나(기본값), SimpleCredentialsMatcher처럼 캐시된 인증 정보와 자격 증명을 검증하는 매처를 설정할 수 있다. 게시일은 2026-11-15이며, 원격 공격이 가능하다고 표기되어 있다.

items.title: A family tree of software job titles
items.content:
For a few years I was ‘Head of DevOps’. Before I got that job title I’d done much the same work under other names, and since then I’ve watched the same work get called SRE, and then it seemed to morph towards platform engineering. If you’ve been in this industry for any length of time you’ll have seen titles come and go like this, and you might have wondered where they all came from.

So I (with the help of Mr Claude) built this family tree of software job titles, from the 1940s to now.

It’s here: ianmiell.github.io/sw-job-title-family-tree

There are 104 titles, from ‘Computer’ (a person, not a machine) at the top to ‘AI Agent / Context Engineer’ at the bottom.

Time runs from top to bottom, in five-year rows. The titles sit in seven coloured columns by family:

A solid arrow means the title grew out of its parent. A dashed arrow means influence, or a common career move. Landmark titles are in bold.

On the site you can click a family to see just that column (here’s Data & AI ), or click a title to get its history, background and connections (here’s SRE ).

The whole thing is one Graphviz file and one JSON file of descriptions. Each title is one line in the .dot file, and the picture is rendered with:

$ dot -Tsvg job_title_family_tree.dot -o job_title_family_tree.svg

Adding a title is three small edits: a node in its family’s column, an entry in the row for its five-year period, and its parent arrows.

A word on the dates. They’re roughly when a title became common , not its first recorded use, and they’re my best estimates, not sourced citations. Some are well known (SRE at Google in 2003, ‘DevOps’ coined in 2009, ‘Data Scientist’ in 2008). Plenty are a ‘c.’ and a shrug.

Drawing it out made a few patterns hard to miss.

1) Coding Started Out as the Clerical Bit

In 1947, Goldstine and von Neumann’s ‘Planning and Coding of Problems’ split the work of using a computer in two: mathematicians planned the problem, and coders translated the plan into machine instructions. Coding was treated as lower-status clerical work, and much of it was done by women.

It turned out that coding eventually became the hard, creative part, and the coder merged into the programmer.

Go back further and it’s stranger still. Several of the first ENIAC programmers were recruited from the Army’s human computers, people whose job was to compute by hand. So the job gave its name to the machine, and its people to programming.

2) Titles Break Apart, Then Join Back Up

The webmaster turned up around 1993, and was often a single person who wrote the HTML, ran the webserver (often a box under a desk), answered the email, and kept the site up (sometimes by kicking it, more often by plugging it back in after kicking it).

By the mid-2000s the title had all but gone, as it was unfashionably ancient. The code went to web developers, the servers to sysadmins, and the content to editors and designers.

Then the web developer split into front-end and back-end around 2005, and the two joined back up again as ‘full-stack’ around 2008.

This is the centralisation/distribution see-saw I’ve written about before , playing out in job titles.

The prompt engineer made headlines in 2023 with a few eye-wateringly well-paid job listings. As the models got better, the skill became part of other jobs, and on the tree it gets absorbed into the AI engineer almost as soon as it appears.

The scrum master is a slower version of the same story: demand peaked in the 2010s, and many organisations have since folded it back into engineering management or delivery roles.

The newest title on the tree is the ‘AI Agent / Context Engineer’ (c. 2025). The description for it currently says “time will tell whether it stays a separate title”. I’m not taking bets.

‘Systems Engineer’ is two different jobs on the tree. At IBM in the 1960s it was a pre-sales role, working with customers to design installations and get them running. In the 1990s, thanks largely to Microsoft’s MCSE…

items.title: cursor:pointer on buttons
items.summary: a11y, css, web
items.content:
Published on: November 13, 2026 Categories: CSSWG  8 , CSS  96 , Opinion Current music: Envy  —   Connected Voice

Three weeks ago, at a CSS Working Grouping meeting, we discussed an issue “ Cursors for base appearance ” , and resolved on the following:

The CSS Working Group just discussed [css-forms-1] Cursors for base appearance, and agreed to the following:

RESOLVED: Adopt cursor rules in the last comment.

SUMMARY: Pointer = “click this thing”, text cursor says “prepare to enter text”, grabbing hand says “drag this”.

One of the rules from the “last comment” mentioned there is

select , option , input [ type = checkbox ], input [ type = radio ],

button , input [ type = button ], input [ type = submit ], input [ type = reset ], input [ type = color ], input [ type = image ], :: file-selector-button {

Or, if we were to remove all non-button selectors,

That is, of course, not a change to the default styles in the browser — this is a rule for elements that will have an  appearance: base-… .

Also note that, this user agent style will be very much overrideable — no  !important .

Anyone who does not like cursor: pointer on buttons and other similar elements, are free to override it to  default (or anything else) in their stylesheets.

The rest of us can, I guess, celebrate? I was always on the side of this decision. I published my  “ Correct Cursor on Active Elements ” article in 2013. In 2017, I opened my first CSSWG issue — “ Change the pointer cursor to indicate any interactive element ” , which led to a change in a non-normative part of the spec.

Since then, I did not see any new arguments in this debate. I will not repeat everything that I argued about, but one of the most common counter-arguments that I read today is “OS does not do it”.

Did you see that “OS”? When was the last time your OS innovated anything in the UI? Did it become easier to use over years?

Many of people with this argument ask, thinking that this will be a good question, something like “What next — change the cursor in the OS?!”.

I mean… Yes? I would be happy with that. When I look at like half of the (non-native) apps in my desktop OS, they have cursor: pointer on interactive elements.

Cinny, Discord, Signal, Slack, Steam, VS Code — some of the apps that I have before me.

When I use apps that do not change the cursor to anything other than default , I cringe.

Default cursor does not communicate anything. It does one job well — point at a specific pixel. It could do more.

In the issue, many people came with dislikes and their arguments against cursor: pointer . I want to aknowledge one argument that I fully agree with — it would be great if buttons and links would have different cursors. And also, regular links should have cursors different from the links that are opened in new tabs.

But if we were to look at those three things:

And then had only two cursors to assign to all of them, I know which ones I will assign to which.

And I will never understand anyone thinking that buttons have more in common with blank space than with links.

items.content_ko: 작성자는 3주 전 CSS 워킹 그룹 회의에서 'Cursors for base appearance' 이슈를 논의했고, 마지막 댓글의 커서 규칙을 채택하기로 결의했다고 전한다. 결의 요지는 포인터는 '이것을 클릭하라', 텍스트 커서는 '입력할 준비를 하라', 잡는 손은 '이것을 드래그하라'는 의미를 갖는다는 것이다. 규칙 대상에는 select, option, 체크박스와 라디오 입력, 여러 종류의 button과 input, ::file-selector-button 등이 포함된다. 이는 브라우저 기본 스타일을 바꾸는 것이 아니라 appearance: base를 가진 요소에 적용되는 규칙이다. 이 사용자 에이전트 스타일은 !important 없이 작성되어 원하지 않는 개발자가 덮어쓸 수 있다고 작성자는 설명한다. 게시일은 2026년 11월 13일이다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: The Original Xbox Turns 25: The Console That Changed Gaming Forever
items.content:
Just after midnight on 15 November 2001, a customer named Eduardo Glucksman walked into the enormous Toys "R" Us store in New York City's Times Square and purchased the very first Xbox. Waiting to greet him was Bill Gates himself, who signed the console before handing it over to its new owner. It was a carefully orchestrated launch for what Microsoft hoped would become one of the most important products in the company's history.

"The future of gaming starts today, and it starts with Xbox," Gates declared in Microsoft's launch announcement.

Microsoft had conquered the world of PC software, but the video game industry was a different beast entirely. Sony's PlayStation 2 was already dominating living rooms, Nintendo was preparing to launch the GameCube in North America just three days later, and Sega had recently withdrawn from the hardware business after the disappointing commercial performance of the Dreamcast.

It was hardly an inviting market for a newcomer. But Microsoft arrived with a machine unlike anything else on sale, backed by extraordinary financial resources and a determination to establish itself as a serious competitor. Whether anyone outside Microsoft actually wanted an Xbox, however, was something even the company itself couldn't be sure of.

The story of the Xbox began with Microsoft's growing concern about Sony and the PlayStation 2. Sony had been positioning its new console as something considerably more ambitious than a machine for playing games. With DVD playback, increasingly sophisticated graphics and the promise of broader entertainment applications, the PlayStation 2 represented a potential challenge to the personal computer's place in the home at all.

Inside Microsoft, a small group of engineers saw an opportunity to turn the company's considerable experience with PC gaming into something new. Among them were Seamus Blackley, Kevin Bachus, Otto Berkes and Ted Hase, who began developing a proposal for a console built around familiar PC components and Microsoft's DirectX technology.

Seamus Blackley, Kevin Bachus, Ted Hase, Otto Berkes. Blackley, whose earlier work included System Shock and Flight Unlimited , would become one of the most recognisable figures associated with the machine's creation.

"We wanted to make a DirectX Box: an Xbox," Blackley explained in a 2020 interview with MachinePix , recalling how the original proposal came together during a flight.

The idea was relatively straightforward. Rather than ask developers to learn an entirely unfamiliar hardware architecture, Microsoft could offer a standardised gaming platform with much of the flexibility and familiarity of an actual PC. Developers would know what hardware they were targeting, allowing them to extract considerably more performance than they could from the unpredictable configurations of contemporary home computers.

Convincing Microsoft's executives was another matter. The company had never manufactured anything quite like this, and the financial implications of entering a market dominated by established Japanese manufacturers were enormous. Blackley has since described considerable internal resistance, including colleagues who reportedly referred to the proposed machine as the "coffin box."

Speaking to GamesBeat in 2021 , he recalled that the difficult part of telling the Xbox story retrospectively was that "at the time nobody knew that it was going to work."

Nevertheless, Gates ultimately approved the project. Microsoft publicly announced its console ambitions in March 2000, and by January 2001, the company was ready to show the world what it had been building.

The original Xbox wasn't all that interested in subtlety. Its enormous black enclosure, distinctive X-shaped upper surface and green central jewel looked almost aggressively different from the understated PlayStation 2 and Nintendo's compact, colourful GameCube.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Project Zero will disclose vulnerabilities 90 days after reporting
items.content:
Since 2021, Project Zero has followed a “90 + 30” vulnerability disclosure policy, allowing vendors up to 90 days to remediate a vulnerability plus an extra 30 days “soak time” for patch rollout. Our goal was to encourage faster patching and give vendors time to deliver patches to users. The advent of AI-assisted vulnerability discovery and exploitation has changed the threat landscape such that the vulnerability remediation timeline encouraged by our disclosure policy is clearly insufficient.

LLMs have increased the speed at which attackers can find and exploit vulnerabilities, alongside the risk that multiple parties, including malicious ones, discover the same bug. A vulnerability reported today presents a much higher immediate risk to users than one reported last year. In this new environment, it is crucial that vendors move towards remediating vulnerabilities faster.

LLMs have also decreased the time it takes for attackers to reverse engineer and exploit a vulnerability based on a patch, to the extent that zero patch-to-exploitation time is a reasonable, though imperfect, model of attacker behavior. Patch soak time is no longer meaningful in a world where attackers can almost immediately determine bug details from a patch, and can put users at risk by creating a false sense of secrecy. “Patch gap” is the time between a fix being released for a security vulnerability and the user installing the relevant update. It is equally crucial that vendors reduce patch gap, either by reducing patch rollout time or using other strategies to protect users while remediation is in progress.

LLMs have also increased the volume of vulnerabilities that Project Zero reports. We are finding several vulnerabilities a week in targets where we once found a few vulnerabilities a year. Aspects of our policy that require vendor negotiation or agreement, including determining whether a bug is fixed and whether grace period applies, are quickly becoming unmanageable.

Today, we are announcing a new vulnerability disclosure policy, created with the following goals in mind:

Encourage faster vulnerability remediation

Allow for the policy to be automated by both Project Zero and vendors

Vulnerabilities will be disclosed X days after they are reported to the vendor.

Starting today, our policy is “Full 90”, i.e. vulnerabilities will be disclosed 90 days after they are reported to the vendor.

On February 2, 2027, we will move to a “Full 60” policy where vulnerabilities are disclosed after 60 days.

On January 3, 2028, we will move to a “Full 30” policy where vulnerabilities are disclosed after 30 days.

We are also removing most ‘special cases’ from our disclosure policy, including grace period and variant policy. The only exceptions to our new policy are:

Vulnerabilities actively exploited in the wild -- ITW vulnerabilities will be handled according to Google’s application security vulnerability disclosure policy

Public vulnerabilities -- Project Zero may make details of a vulnerability public, at our discretion, if the details have already been made public by others

Vendor request -- We will make vulnerability details public if the vendor we reported it to requests it

Project Zero solicited feedback from the vendors we report the most vulnerabilities to as a part of developing this new policy. An overarching concern was that immediately changing the policy could harm users by making unfixed vulnerabilities available to attackers while vendors are in the process of improving their remediation processes and technology. While the benefits of delaying disclosure are declining due to the increased probability that attackers will discover a vulnerability during the embargo period, we still feel there are benefits in the short term.

In addition, vendors mentioned two more subtle concerns. One was that an overly-aggressive disclosure policy would encourage fixing bugs reported under the new policy with more priority, even if they are less severe…

items.content_ko: LLM 덕분에 공격자가 취약점을 찾고 악용하는 속도가 빨라졌고, 악의적인 주체를 포함한 여러 주체가 같은 버그를 동시에 발견할 위험도 커졌다고 설명한다. 패치를 바탕으로 한 리버스 엔지니어링과 악용까지 걸리는 시간도 크게 줄어, 패치 직후 곧바로 악용이 이뤄지는 모델이 합리적이라고 본다. 이 때문에 패치 롤아웃 대기 기간(soak time)은 더 이상 의미가 없다고 밝힌다. 따라서 벤더가 패치를 더 빠르게 제공해야 한다는 입장이다. 원문은 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Anthropomorphic Software
items.summary: culture
items.content:
T here are some programs that I like to call anthropomorphic software. These

programs have copy in the first person that is personified. A distinction I

would like to make is that LLMs and other conversational AI do not count. I

will, however, talk about them at the end.

A familiar example is Git. Have you ever tried to create a commit on a freshly installed system? You might have encountered this error:

Quite personal for a tool whose primary use is to track mistakes.

Start a rebase while Git finds an existing rebase in progress. It also says

In an interactive terminal, mark a revision during bisect before starting the bisect.

My favourite. During git bisect , skip enough commits that Git cannot narrow

Adjacently, Git changelogs too are personified:

"git fsck" learned to catch NUL byte in a commit object as potential error and warn.

CI test was taught to build documentation pages.

The Elm programming language is an extreme example.

I like this effect when used sparingly, unlike Elm.

With this option enabled, sudo will insult you if you enter an incorrect

If you have ever attempted Linux From Scratch, you will know that Bash can say

On September 1, running Nmap with -v makes it wish itself happy birthday.

It also wishes users a merry Christmas on December 25.

If you are aware of any more examples, I would be glad to list them here.

LLM agents are the ultimate version of anthropomorphic software. But agents do

not have to sound human. I force my agents to not speak like humans for my own

sanity. Agents might become the default paradigm of computer user interface in

the future. I will miss anthropomorphic software then.

Most usage of this effect is purely for whimsy and isn't intended to improve

the user experience. Apple's user interface guidelines prescribe avoiding error

items.content_ko: Git의 여러 메시지가 대표 사례로 소개된다. 새로 설치한 시스템에서 커밋할 때 나오는 오류, 이미 진행 중인 rebase가 있을 때의 메시지, bisect 중 건너뛴 커밋 때문에 범위를 좁히지 못하는 상황 등이다. items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Apple is shuttering its 28-year-old online community forum
items.content:
Apple’s online community forum will close on November 20.

On Tuesday night, Apple posted a message to the Apple Support Community announcing the forum’s closure:

The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state.

You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site .

We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products.

For 28 years, the forum has provided Apple users with a way to get quick technical advice about their products. That advice usually came from fellow users, though Apple employees occasionally chimed in. As with any community forum, the helpfulness and accuracy of the advice varied.

Apple reportedly told MacRumors that it is shutting down the forum after evaluating its support strategy and customer needs.

The Apple Support Community dates to 1998, when the online forum was known as Apple Tech Exchange. Two years later, Apple renamed the community forum to Apple Discussions. In 2011 , Apple revamped the forum, adding dedicated communities for specific devices and the ability to track responses to posted questions, while renaming it Apple Support Communities. By 2022, the forum was called Apple Support Community, as MacRumors noted this week.

Based on yesterday’s announcement, it seems Apple now prefers that its customers rely on official Apple employees for technical support. The forum may also have become less popular as rival forums grow, including Reddit and the technical support communities on the MacRumors and AppleInsider forums.

Scharon is a Senior Technology Reporter at Ars Technica writing news, reviews, and analysis on consumer gadgets and services. She's been reporting on technology for over 10 years, with bylines at Tom’s Hardware, Channelnomics, and CRN UK.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: FreeBSD bhyve Live Migration: Moving VMs Between Hosts
items.summary: freebsd, virtualization
items.content:
This project presents a first working state for live migration of bhyve guests on FreeBSD 15.1. A running amd64 guest can move between two hosts over TCP while continuing to run; it is paused only for the final stop-and-copy phase. The work builds on bhyve's experimental snapshot support and adds dirty-page tracking in the vmm kernel module together with a migration protocol in bhyve and bhyvectl.

Live migration of a VM in FreeBSD with bhyve

I previously discussed the state of bhyve live migration, its historical development, existing limitations, and why it matters for the future of FreeBSD virtualization in my article bhyve on FreeBSD and VM Live Migration – Quo vadis? .

The goal is deliberately practical: make it possible to test, discuss, and improve a real implementation rather than discuss live migration only in the abstract. The current code and test tooling are being published as a WIP RFC so that the next steps can be shaped in the open. A more detailed demonstration of a VM being live migrated can be watched on my YouTube channel .

Live migration is an important building block for enterprise virtualisation. It enables host maintenance, hardware replacement, load balancing, and failure-domain management with far less disruption to workloads. It is also central to the Sylve project, which aims to offer a Proxmox-like virtualisation solution for FreeBSD. Migration is not an optional convenience in that kind of platform; it is one of the capabilities that makes clustered operations practical.

It is equally important for BoxyBSD, where I offer free BSD-based VPS instances to individuals. Without a credible migration path, routine host work can require a guest outage. That makes live migration a current show stopper for the project, and is why this work is being pushed toward a testable, reviewable state.

The source starts with a pre-copy phase. It sends populated guest memory, then repeatedly obtains a bitmap of pages changed since the previous scan and sends only those pages. Once the remaining dirty set fits the configured downtime target, stops shrinking, or reaches the configured round limit, bhyve pauses the guest and its devices. It then sends the final dirty pages and the existing snapshot state for the vCPUs, kernel state, and emulated devices.

The destination validates the basic VM geometry, receives memory and state, restores it, and reports that it is ready. Only then does the source send GO , the commit point. Before GO , a failed migration can resume the source guest. The destination does not start the guest if it does not receive that commit message. A warm, stop-and-copy mode is available too, which is useful both as a fallback and as a comparison baseline.

Pre-copy and warm migration: live pre-copy is configurable with downtime and maximum-round controls; explicit stop-and-copy migration is also supported.

Multi-vCPU protocol support: the migration handshake carries the guest vCPU count, the destination refuses a count mismatch, and all guest vCPUs are paused and resumed as part of migration. The published test bed has primarily exercised a one-vCPU guest, so multi-vCPU stress and race testing remain required before making broader claims.

Memory consistency checks: dirty-page tracking covers guest and mapped emulation writes through page dirty state, while vmm write holds are recorded separately. The test workload rewrites and verifies guest memory and reports any missing or stale page as a mismatch. Repeated ping-pong migrations have been used to check that the workload continues without errors.

items.title: Disk encryption on NetBSD - achieving secrecy
items.content:
These are two threat models for which disk encryption is the answer:

The device is stolen or lost and its contents must remain secret.

The device is tampered with, and all attempts at tampering must render it unusable.

Right now, we will focus on the first threat model. It is very difficult to build a tamper-proof system, and you need to worry about tamper-proofing your hardware, depending on what kind of actor is a realistic threat.

If we want to keep data on the system secret, we must first consider which data is worth protecting. On a NetBSD system, our data can be grouped into two broad categories:

Does the /bin/sh executable downloaded from the NetBSD FTP server contain any sensitive information?

On a BSD system, due to the separation of the base system and packages, many root file system directories are mostly unmodified outside of upgrades. In a properly configured system, nearly all system daemons and user applications are not going to be running as root , so won’t have permission to modify or create files in /bin .

We can reasonably assume that /bin/sh is the same binary that every other NetBSD user is running. A user may even opt to make directories containing such system files read-only.

The operating system needs to be able to load files to boot. [citation needed]

This makes "true" full disk encryption difficult to achieve without specialized hardware, since the user needs some way to enter a password or an encryption key, and can’t do so without some form of software running on their computer. NetBSD also needs to store some amount of metadata about the encrypted partition on the disk, such as information on how to generate a secure 256-bit key from a 24 character password.

It is common for Unix systems to use shared libraries, which are loaded by programs to access system functionality. If these become unavailable, for example, by /usr/lib going missing, it becomes much harder to use the system. Familiarize yourself with the standard utilities in /rescue which don’t need working shared libraries to be useful.

The cryptographic algorithms that get standardized by the US government tend to be

This carries a performance penalty. As a result, many modern CPUs include implementations of ciphers like AES in hardware. For those that don’t, there’s alternative ciphers like

And which are necessary for the OS to load?

On a normal NetBSD system, several directories have a high chance of being modified during system operation:

/var - log files, system-wide databases (e.g. mail notifications), crash dumps…

/root - configuration files relevant to the root user account

/usr/pkg and /usr/local - where third-party software is installed

/etc - init scripts, system-wide configuration for the base system

A simple approach might be to encrypt /home . However, this might not be enough for some users. Although the crash directory can be easily changed with

a crash dump contains a snapshot of system memory which might be sensitive. If any servers have been run on the system, the log files might be sensitive. Mail sent to users (e.g. about their interrupted vi sessions and associated backups) might reveal sensitive file names.

approach, which uses only a small unencrypted ramdisk to pivot to an encrypted file system. However, this modifies the system startup routines significantly and may make certain rescue options harder. So, it’s worth asking whether there’s an approach that is somewhere in the middle, and still uses the standard NetBSD installation and boot process. Many BSD systems use separate file system partitions for /usr and /var , and this is a standard configuration supported by the NetBSD installer.

/etc is a harder problem to solve, since it contains files necessary to boot the system. However, on a typical desktop system, many files in /etc remain untouched.
