items.title: Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax
items.content:
The architecture from the DeepSeek-V3 technical report in 190 lines of pure JAX , pretrained from scratch on a MacBook Air on public-domain detective fiction.

No Flax, no Equinox, no PyTorch. Params are plain dicts of arrays and every part of the model is a function you can read top to bottom in deepseek_v3.py .

Read the write-up: DeepSeek V3 in 190 lines of pure JAX , with diagrams, the code explained piece by piece, and the results.

Caches one small latent per token instead of full keys and values: 480 → 144 numbers per token per layer here

One rotary key shared by all heads, kept outside the compressed latent

1 shared expert that always runs + 16 routed experts, top-4 per token

A per-expert bias nudges routing toward idle experts; it changes which experts are picked, not their weights

The small complementary loss from the paper (α = 1e-4)

An extra module also predicts the token after next, weighted λ = 0.3 in the loss

bf16 compute on f32 master weights; prefill + decode with the MLA cache

One run of the default config on a MacBook Air M5 (24 GB):

36.2M parameters, 13.6M active per token

207 books, 21.7M training tokens (Hammett repeated 3×); validation is held-out crime fiction

12,000 steps, ~98M tokens (~4.5 epochs), ~2.6 h

5.7–6.9% per expert (even is 6.25%), at step 2000

With balancing on and off, validation loss at step 2000 was the same (3.921 vs 3.923). The bias evens out the experts without costing anything, which is the paper's claim.

Its own words, from the prompt "The fog came in off the":

The fog came in off the bay, and the great trees were spreading and the stars were shining.

This is an architecture demo, not a strong language model. See the write-up for what worked, what didn't, and what's missing.

The v1.0 release has the exact checkpoint and data from the published run. After installing (step 1):

curl -L -o runs/main/ckpt.pkl https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/ckpt.pkl # 138 MB

curl -L -o data/tokenizer.json https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/tokenizer.json

.venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt " The fog came in off the " --num 3

The checkpoint is a Python pickle, which can run code when loaded. Only load checkpoints from sources you trust.

You need an Apple Silicon Mac, Python 3.12 and uv . The published run used 24 GB of memory. No Mac? See Running on CPU .

git clone https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax.git && cd deepseek-v3-jax

uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt

Every version in requirements.txt is pinned. jax-metal 0.1.1 only works with jax==0.4.34 , so don't upgrade JAX.

JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/pytest tests.py -q # 39 passed

.venv/bin/python smoke_metal.py # optional: what jax-metal supports on your Mac

In smoke_metal.py , "grad through 2-axis contraction" fails on jax-metal 0.1.1. That's expected, and the model is written to avoid it.

This downloads the 207 books in sources.txt (~120 MB, about 7 minutes), cleans them, trains an 8,192-token BPE tokenizer and writes data/train.bin , data/val.bin and data/tokenizer.json . It should print:

train: 211 docs, 83.4M chars, 21.69M tokens

The published run's data had these hashes:

shasum -a 256 data/train.bin data/val.bin data/tokenizer.json

d37aca97e707bb81b6e4d266cc1adfd1f3e3556457c6eb724e495118a734e0bb data/train.bin

b7ac285b115e6793b5d36aa5b4bc6e81a5fccfc7af0908a306d3828ebca9c31c data/val.bin

c5a142b4006a967c880dda44ad792719d53c16d947da3b6c2332d6132d9967cc data/tokenizer.json

You will most likely get different hashes. The Hammett books are pinned to exact Standard Ebooks commits and come out identical, but Project Gutenberg files can't be pinned, and Gutenberg has since re-issued 28 of the 203 books with small edits (mostly accents stripped, like "José" → "Jose"). The token counts come out the same, so training should behave the same.

items.content_ko: 토큰마다 키와 값 전체 대신 작은 잠재 벡터 하나만 캐시하는 MLA 방식을 쓰며, 토큰당 레이어별 저장 수가 480에서 144로 줄어든다고 한다. 회전 키(rotary key)는 모든 헤드가 공유하며 압축된 잠재 벡터 바깥에 둔다. 항상 실행되는 공유 전문가 1개와 라우팅 전문가 16개를 두고 토큰마다 상위 4개를 고르며, 전문가별 편향으로 유휴 전문가 쪽으로 라우팅을 유도하되 가중치는 바꾸지 않는다. 논문의 보조 손실(α=1e-4)을 포함하고, 다음다음 토큰을 예측하는 추가 모듈을 손실에 λ=0.3 가중치로 반영한다. 연산은 bf16, 마스터 가중치는 f32로 하며 MLA 캐시를 이용한 프리필과 디코딩을 지원한다. 학습 데이터는 탐정 소설 207권, 약 2,170만 토큰(Hammett 작품은 3회 반복)이다. 검증은 보류된 데이터로 진행된다고 하나 원문이 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA’s ground stop
items.content:
Work to replace old copper wire led to the FAA’s ground stop

Issues with a new router related to a fiber optic upgrade grounded thousands of flights on Friday.

Issues with a new router related to a fiber optic upgrade grounded thousands of flights on Friday.

A view of an information board at the Chicago O’Hare International Airport, filled with waiting passengers on November 13, 2026. Anadolu via Getty Images

Terrence O'Brien is the Verge’s weekend editor. He’s covered the tech industry for over 18 years and knows a thing or two about synths.

At a press conference today, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said that Friday’s nationwide ground stop ordered by the FAA was related to work replacing outdated copper wire with a fiber optic line at a “remote FAA facility.” The secretary said that this was “routine maintenance,” rather than the result of a major modernization effort. He told reporters that it was “such an old wire that it was being discontinued, meaning that line was going to get shut down,” necessitating the upgrade.

What wasn’t clear, according to Secretary Duffy, was the root cause of the problem. He said that it could have been faulty hardware, a misconfigured router, or “incompetence” on the part of contractor L3Harris. Regardless, what followed was the newly installed router “flooding” other routers in the Air Traffic Control system. Duffy said that there were “over 1,000 connection attempts every 4 to 5 seconds,” causing disruption to radar feeds and communication with planes.

Secretary Duffy also took the opportunity to call on additional funding from Congress for modernizing the Air Traffic Control system , and to tout the work the FAA has done so far. “We are building, we are building safely, but we are building fast,” he said, but said that Congress had only given him a “partial payment” to complete the necessary work.

In a statement posted to their site, L3Harris said:

L3Harris has been modernizing the communications infrastructure supporting the National Airspace System in close coordination with the FAA. With safety and reliability as our highest priorities, L3Harris, together with its telco partners and the FAA, has completed more than 70% of the planned airspace communications conversion from legacy copper wires to a fiber optic system. We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the Nov. 13 ground stop of our nation’s air travel. L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.

Update November 14th: Added a statement from L3Harris.

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

items.title: We're Asking an Appeals Court to Require a Warrant for ALPR Searches
items.content:
Today , along with the ACLU, EFF filed an amicus brief in the Sixth Circuit court of appeals in United States v. Sturdivant , a case where police warrantlessly tracked a suspect’s movements using Automated License Plate Reader (ALPR) data. Our brief details the vast, interconnected network of ALPRs that constantly track drivers around the country and argues that this tracking is a “search” under the meaning of the Fourth Amendment.

Sturdivant involves a series of robberies in and around Cleveland, Ohio. Using surveillance camera footage, police identified the make, model, and color of the robber’s car, but they did not know its license plate number. After running an open-ended search of two ALPR databases, Flock and ELSAG, officers learned a car belonging to the defendant had been tracked near sites of the robberies, eventually leading to his arrest. Faced with a motion to suppress the ALPR evidence, the district court held that Mr. Sturdivant had no reasonable expectation of privacy in his license plate number because it could be observed by members of the public, and that therefore he had no Fourth Amendment interest in not having his car tracked in public places.

But ALPRs are simply not comparable to observing an individual license plate on a passing car. As we’ve explained in many amicus briefs and in our lawsuits directly challenging ALPR use in San Jose, California and Wisconsin , ALPRs give law enforcement “ a virtual time machine to view suspects’, or anyone else’s, past movements (and much more) with just the click of a button.” Just last month, a federal district court agreed and held that ALPRs are a “ form of indiscriminate mass surveillance” that can violate the Fourth Amendment.

We hope the Sixth Circuit will reverse the lower court in this case and hold that ALPR searches require a warrant.

Sturdivant 사건의 조언서를 제출했다. 이 사건은 오하이오주 클리블랜드 일대에서 일어난 연쇄 강도 사건과 관련되어 있다. 경찰은 감시 카메라 영상으로 강도가 탄 차량의 제조사, 모델, 색상은 파악했지만 번호판은 알지 못했다. 이후 경찰은 Flock과 ELSAG 두 ALPR 데이터베이스를 광범위하게 검색했고, 피고인 차량이 강도 현장 근처에서 추적된 사실을 확인해 체포에 이르렀다. 지방법원은 번호판은 공공장소에서 누구나 볼 수 있으므로 피고인에게 번호판에 대한 합리적 사생활 기대가 없고, 따라서 공공장소에서 차량이 추적되는 것에 대해 수정헌법 제4조상의 이익도 없다고 판단했다. EFF는 ALPR이 서로 연결된 광범위한 네트워크를 통해 전국의 운전자를 지속적으로 추적하고 있으며, 이런 추적은 제4조의 「수색」이라고 주장한다. 원문 본문은 중간에 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Reintroducing Spaces
items.summary: programming
items.content:
Atproto Spaces are a new primitive in the atproto stack. We just launched the protocol in alpha . Check it out, give the blogpost a read, and sign up on the alpha PDS!

My own intuition around this protocol has been consistently evolving as I’ve worked on it. You can trace much of that through the Permissioned Data Diary series I wrote during the design process. Now with some time and perspective, I wanted to zoom back out, look at the design of Spaces and take a shot at succinctly motivating them as a new primitive.

Our initial goal was to extend atproto to work for non-public data. Specifically though, we wanted to enable social use cases . Which is to say that the protocol isn’t intended for just bookmarks or even “gated posts”, but needs to work for large multi-user social contexts such as a 100k user forum.

Our next goal is to maintain existing atproto intuition . Users publish records, those records are canonically stored in the user’s PDS, authority rests in the author’s DID, and applications crawl PDSes and sync data to build their own views. Succeeding in this means that many difficult questions around things like moderation and credible exit are already answered!

An extension of that goal is that it must be atmospheric . I use “atmospheric” to refer to the same underlying data getting remixed across apps in different lights. Think: Bluesky posts showing up as comments under a standard.site blog or rpg.actor characters walking across the bottom of your streamplace stream. Atmospheric features are the features that make this network feel like one deeply integrated experience rather than a bunch of isolated apps that just happen to have the same login.

And finally, the protocol needs to be secure and legible to users . This protocol enables many-to-many sharing in a multi-app, multi-pds, multi-modality network. That’s a lot of variables! This all comes to a head in the OAuth consent screen. And being able to communicate what an app is allowed to do in a concrete way in just a couple sentences is absolutely critical to the Atmosphere being broadly approachable and usable.

Spaces are our new primitive. Each space represents a shared social context. They’re a simple and concrete mechanism for organizing and permissioning data. Built around an abstraction of locality, each record is “in” a space and only one space. Each space is explicitly tied to a particular modality and owned by a single entity.

a diagram abstractly showing a space with three records in it

As we explored this new primitive, we realized that it seems uniquely able to thread the needle on all of our design goals.

Spaces are a deeply social primitive (fitting for a social networking protocol!). Spaces are not really about “who do I, as an individual, share this piece of content with”. Spaces are meant for establishing a shared social context . Records are in that context, and everyone with access to that context has the exact same view over it. It’s a shared common reality, and this shared sense of space allows for truly social applications.

We’ve started describing spaces as “mini atprotos” (btw if that sounds heavy duty, don’t worry spaces are actually very lightweight & low overhead). That analogy turns out to hold startlingly well. Not only does it help communicate the new primitive, but it also has the huge benefit that almost all of the really difficult questions of using the protocol for real-world social networks can be answered pretty simply: they’re the same as existing atproto! From moderation to account migration to the role of applications, intuition from public atproto maps very closely to spaces.

Spaces are quite legible. Of course this isn’t a gimme, the Atmosphere is pretty novel, and we’re all familiar with the new challenges of communicating this novel network to users. However, as I mentioned, this question of legibility comes to a head in the OAuth screen. In a context like that, describing “spaces” is much more grounded than…

Update 5: Instagram is now leaking recovery email and phone numbers linked to an account.

Seems like every day a new security issue crops up at Instagram.

Instagram Exposing Linked Email and Phone Number

Update 4: A new report suggests that Instagram accounts may be vulnerable to coordinated mass-report abuse. According to the claim, when a newly created account is routed through a Los Angeles-based VPN and then submits a specific mix of reports in scam and fraud category, the targeted account can allegedly be banned without any human review.

Instagram Account Banning by AI by Reporting Scam and Fraud (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 3: Meta’s apparent fix for the AI bot vulnerability is difficult to take seriously. Instead of fully disabling the risky functionality, they reportedly removed it from the visible interface while leaving the underlying API endpoint accessible. Hiding the button may stop regular users from seeing the feature, but it does nothing if attackers can still reach the same workflow directly through the API.

Meta Hid AI Chatbot from UI (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 2: Yet another Instagram account-takeover trick is reportedly being abused, this time involving Meta’s AI chatbot. Sellers are allegedly using modified Instagram builds on Android emulators like BlueStacks, then manipulating the AI with hidden characters and carefully worded prompts to force username changes. The method is reportedly being used to grab rare OG handles, including one-letter usernames, and handle-monitoring bots have already flagged several suspicious swaps.

New Instagram AI Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Update 1: A new exploit, which is even worse than this one is currently doing rounds on telegram. Details unknown at this time. Unpatched at the time of writing.

New Instagram Unpatched Exploit (Source: X/Twitter)

Allegedly, the new method is via Facebook recovery. Apparently, prompting Meta AI to turn on “Development Mode” and attaching proof of account compromise along with email works. More details awaited.

There’s a version of this story where it reads like a hypothetical from a conference talk. An AI agent with elevated backend privileges. A natural language interface sitting in front of account-level APIs. No hard authentication gate before executing state changes. Someone in the audience raises their hand and says, “that’s a disaster waiting to happen.” Everyone nods.

That hypothetical played out in production over the weekend.

A logical flaw in Meta’s AI-powered Instagram account recovery assistant let attackers bypass two-factor authentication entirely not by cracking a code or intercepting an SMS, but by talking the chatbot into doing the work for them. Prominent researchers woke up locked out of their own profiles.

items.title: Let Over Lambda, the legendary Lisp book is free to read online
items.content:
Let Over Lambda (ISBN 978-1-4357-1275-1, 376+iv pp.) is one of the most hardcore computer programming books out there. Starting with the fundamentals, it describes the most advanced features of the most advanced language: C OMMON L ISP . The point of this book is to expose you to ideas that you might otherwise never be exposed to.

This book is about macros, that is programs that write programs. Macros are what make lisp the greatest programming language in the world. When used properly, macros enable amazing feats of abstraction, programmer productivity, and code efficiency and security that are unheard of elsewhere. Macros let you do things you simply cannot do in other languages.

If you are looking for a dry coding manual that re-hashes common-sense techniques in whatever langue du jour, this book is not for you. This book is about pushing the boundaries of what we know about programming. While this book teaches useful macro skills that can help solve your programming problems today and now, it has also been designed to be entertaining and inspiring. If you have ever wondered what lisp or even programming itself is really about, this is the book you have been looking for.

2026 update: Let Over Lambda was published in 2008, to align with the 50th anniversary of Lisp's invention in 1958. A lot has changed since then, in both Lisp and programming practice in general. Although my thinking and opinions have evolved since, I still believe the book holds up well as a tutorial and explanation of why Lisp so special. Going forward, the entire book is free to read online ( HTML , PDF ). Happy lisping!

온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

items.title: How did Woz write the Apple 1 BASIC before building the computer?
Solving the fox game
items.summary: math
items.content:
Christoffer Stjernlöf posted about the Fox Game ,

an old Norse asymmetric board game (seemingly also called “halatafl”) where

twenty sheep try to outsmart two foxes and get to the other side.

His AI uncovered some interesting insights, but left the question open as of whether the

foxes or the sheep actually win with perfect play (the general sentiment

in his family was that winning with the foxes was easy). This was too tempting

for me to leave on the table, so I set out to make a strong solve.

Since I don't know this game myself, I've stayed with the rules he describes

even when they differ from e.g. Wikipedia

(in particular, I do not use forced fox jumps, or multi-jumps); the only

real change is that I don't have a 40-move draw rule, any position that is

a forced win for one of the sides would be a win no matter how long it would

take. (I consider this just an implementation detail in his AI, although

morally, I consider a draw a loss for the sheep.) You might want to read

his post to get the full rules, because I'm not going to repeat them here.

The results first: The sheep win with perfect play, even with only 19 sheep

(remove one on the flank), or 18 if they are allowed to go first. Even with

only 9 sheep (the minimum possible that isn't an instant win for the foxes),

the sheep can force a draw right from the start. With one fox, 11 sheep

suffice for a forced win. (The draw margin is seemingly so large because

one fox can just camp in the last spot in the pen, and it's hard to force

it away without getting harassed by the other fox, unless you have lots of sheep.)

The rest is about the implementation. I'll skip over a lot of wrong turns,

and unsurprisingly, there were a lot of bugs to iron out, but hopefully,

it got to a good place in the end. :-) I started out trying to make something

very simple, and it worked for the first few cases, but then things got

more complicated than I would have liked in the end. Still only at ~1000

lines of code, though, with no dependencies.

The board has 33 squares. I tried a few different ways of represent the state

of the game, and ended up on a simple bitboard representation: There's a

64-bit bitmap representing where there are sheep, and another bitmap

representing where there are foxes. Since there's plenty of room in there,

I use a spare bit to represent side-to-move. This is compact (which mattered

a lot earlier on, but not as much later), easy to iterate over, and has

little redundancy, so it's easy to keep valid. You need fast 64-bit population

count and bit-scan instructions, but a) that's common now everywhere,

and b) I decided fairly early that I wanted to require BMI2 anyway.

The bit order mostly doesn't matter; I just started at top-left and went

from there. All it really influences is square iteration order. There's

a small tweak in that I store the right half of the board mirrored

(reverse x order) for symmetry purposes; more on that below.

I just typed in every possible move from every square into an array,

then verified by generating some SVGs that I hadn't made any typos (I had).

In retrospect, I should have done something more automated; it would have

The moves for sheep are just “you can go to X, Y or Z”. The moves

for foxes are “you can go to X or Y, or you can go to Z if there's

a sheep at W (which will be eaten)”. The move generator mostly just looks up

the source square and tests every move. For the sheep, I make an easy

test using bitboards; for the foxes, I could probably do something

similar, but the jump moves proved a bit tricky (even with PEXT/PDEP)

This is the part that really determines the geometry of the board

(apart from debugging display). Everything else is pretty much geometry-agnostic.

There's a little over 2^41 possible board states (this includes some

illegal positions as well as some situations that could never arise

during actual gameplay, such as a fox being stuck at C1 with a row

of sheep…

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: COMAC's electric aircraft completes first piloted test flight
items.content:
China's first domestically developed 10-metric-ton-class electric commercial aircraft, the CE-25A, completed its first piloted test flight in Binzhou, Shandong province, on Saturday, marking another milestone in the development of electric aircraft for short-haul commercial travel.

The aircraft, developed by Commercial Aircraft Corp of China, carried two pilots and a flight test engineer. The test lasted 57 minutes and 46 seconds, including 16 minutes and 38 seconds in the air, during which the aircraft covered 60.4 kilometers.

The aircraft performed normally and all test results met expectations, COMAC said in a statement.

The CE-25A is COMAC's first electric commercial aircraft, designed to carry 19 passengers on commercial flights between cities. It has a maximum takeoff weight of 10 metric tons, a cruising speed of 300 kilometers per hour, a cruising altitude of 2,400 meters, and a range of 400 kilometers.

The aircraft is powered by a distributed electric ducted-fan propulsion system mounted on its wings.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.
